purpose: One daily newspaper, not a stream of links or a popularity contest
selectionPrinciples: Keep evidence quality separate from importance. Quality is a hard floor, not a proxy for reader relevance.
Importance combines consequences, genuinely new information, personal relevance and timeliness; explain these rather than treating a numeric score as objective truth.
Prioritize consequential AI and software developments, useful practitioner insights, markets, macroeconomics, completed or proposed deals and regulation.
Major world events, governance changes and public-health developments must not be crowded out by high-volume technology sources.
Prefer one strongest account per event. Additional reports must contribute distinct evidence; an update must state what materially changed.
An older high-value analysis or complete podcast can qualify if not previously published; preserve its real date and do not portray it as breaking news.
Keep sports concise: major developments, results and standings rather than routine speculation.
Do not fill sectors or publisher quotas with weak stories, product advertising, stock tips or routine announcements.
Do not infer the reader's political preferences or optimize for agreement, outrage or engagement.
Use an independent prepublication event checklist and expose unresolved access and coverage gaps in the private audit. Never invent evidence to fill a gap.
